notes: §1985:VI.6.2.3 GR5 gives exponentiation three rules: a) a zero base needs an exponent greater than zero, else the size error condition; b) of a positive and a negative real result the positive one is returned; c) 'If no real number exists as the result of the evaluation, the size error condition exists'. a) and b) are CobolIntrinsics.CheckPowRule6's zero-base screen and Math.Pow's principal root (0 ** 0 is a size error, 4 ** 0.5 is 2). c) is the COBOL-85 arm of DialectBehavior.NegativeBaseRequiresIntegerExponent (kb/Work PB5186; VCR row 7.67): ExpressionBinder.BindPower sets BoundPower.NegativeBaseRealRoots at 85, NumericRenderer.Power then passes the exponent EXACTLY (CobolIntrinsics.PowNativeReal(double, CobolExact), its checked twin, or CobolExact.PowReal's negativeBaseRealRoots arm for an exact operand), and CobolExact.HasOddDenominator decides whether the exponent is p/q in lowest terms with q odd: then the result is the real number +-|b|**(p/q), negative for p odd, else the size error. Measured at --std 85: (-32) ** 0.2 = -2, (-32) ** 0.4 = 4, (-32) ** -0.2 = -0.5, MAX (-32 -40) ** 0.6 = -8, IF (-32) ** 0.2 < 0 is true, and (-4) ** 0.5 takes the SIZE ERROR phrase with the receiver unchanged.

next.reason: Rules a and b are kept in §2023:8.8.1.2 GR6 a) and b) (zero base needs a positive exponent; of a positive and a negative real result the positive is returned), the size error condition still raised (EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION is set but checking is off for a 1985 program). Rule c differs: 1985 'If no real number exists as the result of the evaluation, the size error condition exists'; 2023 'If the value of an expression to be raised to a power is less than zero, the evaluation of the exponent shall result in an integer. Otherwise ... the size error condition is raised'. (-32) ** 0.2 has the real result -2, so 1985 returns -2 while 2023 raises size error. The 0 ** 0 rules of 8.8.1.4.4 and 8.8.1.5.4 belong to standard-binary and standard-decimal arithmetic, which a 1985 program never selects.
